To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated a Tm:LLF thin disk laser with high output power, efficiency, and tuning range, which is the first of its kind.
we demonstrated the first diode-pumped 1.9-µm thin-disk laser based on Tm3+:LLF.
we demonstrate the first 1.9µm Tm3+LiLuF4 disk laser with a slope efficiency of up to 49% and 40% optical-to-optical conversion efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the realization of a high-power Tm3+:Lu2O3 thin-disk laser at 2.0 μm and the development of a high-power, diode-pumped, Tm3+:YLF thin-disk laser operating in the eye-safe spectral region.
the development of a compact and high-power laser system operating at 1.9-2.0 μm.
the development of high-power, diode-pumped, Tm3+:LLF thin-disk lasers for applications in the 1.9–2.1 µm spectral range.

the presented Tm:LiLuF4 laser system is the most efficient thin-disk laser operating around 1.95 μm to the best of our knowledge.

the presented Tm3+:LLF thin-disk laser represents the first demonstration of this kind of laser and that it is a promising concept for future high-power Tm3+:Lu2LuF7 lasers.

the thin-disk geometry is a very promising approach for the realization of high-power Tm3+:based solid-state laser sources in the eye-safe wavelength range.
we have developed a new laser material for thin-disk lasers and that the first demonstration of such a laser is a milestone.
